seoTitle: Annotate PDF Online - Add Text, Highlights and Drawings
metaDescription: Add text notes, highlight boxes, rectangles, lines and freehand strokes to a PDF as real annotations or burned in. Private, in your browser.
intro: Mark up a PDF with text, highlights, boxes, lines and ink strokes by writing one line per annotation. The file never leaves your browser.
why:
Reviewing a PDF usually means a heavy editor or an upload. Here you describe each mark in one short line and the tool adds it to the file:

1 text 72 80 14 red Reviewed puts red 14-point text on page 1; all highlight 72 100 200 16 yellow draws a yellow highlight box on every page; rect, line and draw add outlines, straight lines and freehand strokes (a list of x,y points). Positions are in points (1/72 inch) from the top-left corner of the page as displayed, so they also work on rotated pages and pages with a crop box.

Choose between real PDF annotations (FreeText, Highlight, Square, Line and Ink objects with appearance streams, which viewers can still select and delete) and burning the marks into the page content, which is permanent and shows identically everywhere. Text uses Helvetica with Western European characters; other characters become a question mark.

Typing coordinates is the keyboard-friendly alternative to drawing with a mouse, and it is precise. Existing content, forms and bookmarks are kept. Digital signatures are invalidated by any change. Nothing is uploaded.
howTo: Write one annotation per line in the box, using the formats shown, for example 1 text 72 80 14 red Reviewed.
Decide whether to burn the marks into the page.
Download the annotated PDF and check it in your viewer.

faq.q: How do I know which coordinates to use?
faq.a: Measure from the top-left of the page as displayed: x to the right, y downward, in points. A US Letter page is 612 by 792 points, A4 is 595 by 842. The page size tool lists the exact values.

Text (FreeText), highlight, rectangle (Square), straight line and freehand ink. Sticky notes, stamps, underline, strike-through, arrows and images are not supported. Highlights use a multiply blend so text beneath stays readable.

faq.q: Annotations or burned in: which one?
faq.a: Real annotations stay editable in viewers and can be removed again, but some simple viewers draw them less faithfully. Burned-in marks are part of the page and always display the same, but cannot be removed later.

faq.q: Does it work on scanned or rotated pages?
faq.a: Yes. Scans are just pages with an image, and the position maths handles page rotation and crop boxes. Encrypted files are refused: unlock them first.

faq.q: Can I draw with the mouse?
faq.a: Not here. You enter stroke points as x,y pairs. That keeps it keyboard accessible and exact, but is slower for long freehand lines.
